sections.h2: Where does Tuscola County record deeds?
sections.html:
Deeds, mortgages and other land instruments are recorded at the Tuscola County Register of Deeds, 125 W. Lincoln Street, Suite 400, Caro, MI 48723, in the Purdy Building. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and closes from noon to 1:00 p.m., on weekends and on holidays. The phone is 989-672-3840 and the email is registerofdeeds@tuscolacounty.org.

Documents can be handed in or mailed. Correct fees and a self-addressed stamped envelope must come with a mailed document, and the office takes checks, money orders and cash. A check needs the account holder's and bank's name and address printed on it. Wrong fees cause a rejection, so check the document and the amount before sending.

Caro is the county seat, and Vassar is the only other city. The county sits in the Thumb region of Michigan, along the Cass River, with M-15, M-24, M-25, M-46, M-81 and M-138 crossing it.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Tuscola County?
sections.html:
Recording any deed, mortgage, lis pendens, certified copy or other instrument costs a flat $30.00. Extra charges apply when one document touches several earlier records.

Tuscola County Register of Deeds fees, from the office's Fees for Copies and Recording page
ItemAmount
Recording a deed, mortgage, lis pendens or other instrument$30.00 flat
Each additional liber and page assigned or discharged, or indexed and posted$3.00 added
Copy of a real estate record$1.00 per page
Certification of a copy$5.00 per document
State or federal tax lien search certificate$3.00 per name

Of the recording fee, $4.00 goes to the Michigan State Survey and Remonumentation fund. That $4.00 is not charged on fixture filings, state or federal liens, state deeds, plats or tax reversion documents. Copies must be paid for when you buy them, and mailed copy requests need the liber and page.

sections.h2: What must happen at the Treasurer before a warranty deed is recorded?
sections.html:
A tax certificate must come first. Before the Register of Deeds will record a warranty deed, a land contract assignment with a warranty clause, or a master deed for a condominium, the document goes to the Tuscola County Treasurer for certification under MCLA 211.135, with a $5.00 certification fee.

Once the Treasurer returns the stamped document, send it with all other papers to the Register of Deeds in recording order, with the exact fee. The Treasurer's number for certification questions is 989-672-3890. The recording requirements page also says that documents of conveyance with warranties or covenants must be certified by the county Treasurer that all taxes have been paid before submission.

A seller who owes tax should plan on this step. The title company or the closing attorney usually orders the certificate, so confirm early who is responsible for it.

sections.h2: What does Michigan require on a document before Tuscola County will record it?
sections.html:
The office applies the rules of MCL 565.201 and related sections. A document that misses one of these gets sent back.

  • Original signatures only, with each name typed, stamped or printed beneath it. A fax or copy cannot be recorded.
  • An acknowledgement by a judge, court clerk or notary public for any document that conveys or encumbers Michigan real estate.
  • The grantee's street or post office address and the name and address of the person who drafted the document.
  • A margin of unprinted space of at least 2 1/2 inches at the top of the first page and 1/2 inch on the other sides, black ink, type of at least 10 points, and white paper between 8 1/2 by 11 and 8 1/2 by 14 inches.
  • No more than four sequential digits of a Social Security number.
  • One recordable event per instrument, stated on the first line of print.

A death certificate or court order must be certified to be recordable, and a true copy is refused. The office does not prepare deeds, give legal advice or supply blank forms.

sections.h2: How much is Michigan transfer tax on a Tuscola County sale?
sections.html:
Two transfer taxes apply to a recorded deed: a county tax and a state tax. Under MCL 207.504, a county with fewer than 2,000,000 people charges 55 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500. Under MCL 207.525, the state tax is $3.75 for each $500 or fraction of $500.

The instrument must state the total value of the real property on its face, or an affidavit of value must be attached. The recording requirements page tells filers that tax is collected on the total consideration unless a valid exemption is stated on the document.

  • Both acts exempt instruments where the consideration is under $100, security instruments, leases and certain land contracts.
  • The state act, MCL 207.526, also exempts a conveyance from an individual to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild, and a transfer in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure.
  • The county act's list in MCL 207.505 does not include the family transfer exemption, so ask the office how the county portion applies to a gift to a child.

sections.h2: How do I find or protect records at the Tuscola County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Land record indexes are online from December 1988 to the present, and older records back to 1852 can be researched in the office. Indexes run by grantor and grantee name. The office cannot search by property address or parcel number, and it cannot say when a house was built, since its records cover land only.

Anyone may buy a copy of a recorded document, because recorded documents are public. A free Property Alert service emails you when a document in your name is recorded. The office says it is an alert and not fraud prevention, and a common name can trigger false alarms. Write to or call the office if an alert shows a document you do not recognize.

The register will not do title searches beyond simple ones, and the staff cannot decide who owns a property. That legal conclusion belongs with an attorney or title company.

sections.h2: What if the property taxes on a Tuscola County house are behind?
sections.html:
The Tuscola County Treasurer helps owners with delinquent tax avoid foreclosure and lists options to keep the property, sell it or let foreclosure go ahead. A property in forfeiture is not yet foreclosed. The office adds a title search fee of at least $175 plus the recording fee, and interest rises to 18% (1.5% per month), retroactive to when the tax first became delinquent.

After a year in forfeiture, the property is foreclosed, the owner's interest and all liens are removed and the right to redeem ends. Foreclosed parcels are offered at auction, and the county says details usually appear in early August for the August and October sales. For a bill you dispute, call your township assessor, who also handles Principal Residence, veteran and poverty exemption questions.

Tuscola County had about 52,680 residents in 2025, 86.4% of occupied homes were owner-occupied, and the median value was $149,500 for 2020 to 2024. Median household income was $63,811 and the average commute is 29.6 minutes, a sign of how rural much of the county is.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Tuscola County?
faqs.a: The flat recording fee is $30.00 for a deed, mortgage, lis pendens or other instrument, plus $3.00 for each additional liber and page. Transfer tax is separate and is collected on the total consideration unless an exemption is stated.

faqs.q: Do I need a tax certificate before recording a warranty deed in Tuscola County?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the document to the Tuscola County Treasurer first with the $5.00 certification fee, then submit the stamped document to the Register of Deeds with exact recording fees. The Treasurer's phone is 989-672-3890.

faqs.q: Can I look up a Tuscola County deed by address?
faqs.a: No. The office is not set up to index by address or parcel number. Search by grantor or grantee name, or give the liber and page, and online indexes start December 1, 1988.

faqs.q: Who can get a copy of a recorded Tuscola County deed?
faqs.a: Anyone can, because a recorded document is public. Copies cost $1.00 per page, a certification adds $5.00 per document, and mail requests need a self-addressed stamped envelope.

faqs.q: What are Michigan's transfer tax rates in Tuscola County?
faqs.a: The county rate is 55 cents per $500 of value and the state rate is $3.75 per $500. Both apply to the total value stated on the instrument or in an attached affidavit.
